chunks: And it is narrated from Abū ʿAlī ibn Rāshid, who said:
I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام: “Something is brought to us, and it is said: ‘This belonged to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام and is with us.’ So how should we act?”

So he said: “Whatever belonged to my father عليه السلام by reason of the Imamate, then it is mine; and whatever was other than that, then it is inheritance according to the Book of Allah and the sunnah of His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.”

key_terms.الْإِمَامَةِ: the office and authority of the Imam
key_terms.سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّهِ: the normative practice and teaching of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: the divine law and rulings found in the Qur'an
key_terms.لِأَبِي: referring to the Imam’s father عليه السلام
key_terms.لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: referring to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, the previous Imam

ai.seo_question: How is the property of a previous Imam divided between the next Imam and the legal heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between property attached to the office of the Imam and ordinary personal property. What belongs to the Imam due to the Imamate passes to the next Imam, while other property is treated as inheritance according to the Book of Allah and the sunnah of His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1657 - It is narrated from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Hadi (as)) "We are sometimes brought something, and it is said, 'This belonged to Abu Ja'far (Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Jawad (as)) and is now with us.' What should we do with it?"

The Imam (as) replied: "Whatever belonged to my father (as) due to his position as the Imam is now mine. As for anything else, it is inheritance distributed according to the Book of Allah (swt) and the Sunnah of His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family."
